title.en: Units of length (additional, not in the textbook)

text.en: At the class party, Shelly measures the height of the door with paper strings. Leena and Adi use hand spans to measure the same table. Will they get the same number?

The class is preparing for a party. The picture shows many ways to measure length.
Shelly finds the height of the door using paper strings. Others use hand spans, footsteps or a ruler.
Leena and Adi measure the same table with their own hand spans. Their answers may differ, because their hands are different sizes.
That is why we need a standard unit that is the same for everybody, like a centimetre or a metre.
Colour the shortest paper string red and the longest green. Compare strings by laying them side by side.
Hand spans and footsteps are informal units. Rulers and tapes use formal units.

problem.en: Why do two children get different hand-span counts?

text.en: Everybody's hand is a different size.
A bigger hand covers more, so fewer spans.

prompt.en: Is a hand span a good unit for selling cloth?

points.en: Length can be measured with hand spans, steps and strings.
